PG101.title: The missing delivery
PG101.description: A receipt exists in the warehouse, but has not reached accounts payable.

PG102.title: The approved amendment
PG102.description: A legitimate price change is held until procurement authority is retrieved.

PG103.title: Two gaps, one case
PG103.description: A price amendment and a delivery record must both be obtained.

PG104.title: Evidence arrives later
PG104.description: A reviewer requests a recheck; a delayed receipt then becomes available.

PG105.title: The receipt reuse trap
PG105.description: Two distinct invoices together exceed the delivered and ordered quantity.

PG106.title: The poisoned attachment
PG106.description: A receipt was changed after its content hash was pinned.

PG107.title: Conflicting authority
PG107.description: Two approved amendments disagree; the agent must escalate.

PG108.title: The tolerance trap
PG108.description: A tiny unit difference doubles the total line exposure.

PG109.title: Verified bank change
PG109.description: A bank change needs an authorised vendor-master record, never invoice text.

PG110.title: Unresolved delivery
PG110.description: No authoritative receipt exists; the system must preserve the evidence gap.
